questions: How many devices did you measure, and how many showed the global signatures, the spectral jumps and the zero-bias peaks? You write that the global signatures appear "in all examined devices" (p. 4) and that you "were able to produce a series of devices with two functioning tunnel contacts" (p. 4), but the size of that series isn't given.
Why were the other devices set aside, and was the tunnel-junction yield ("below 50%", p. 5) the only reason?
Which ranges of Bx, VG and field angle did you measure beyond the ones shown, for example Bx above 4 T in devices B and C, or VG outside the window of Fig. 4?
What does the second-best device or dataset look like, beyond A, B and C, for example a two-probe device that was set aside or another cooldown of device B?

What were the tunnel-contact resistances of devices A, B and C, and what filter resistance did you subtract in the two-terminal measurements? Your Methods say the contacts "typically exhibit resistances exceeding 100 kΩ" (p. 5), while Fig. S1a shows about 0.6 to 1.4 e^2/h at 2 mV, roughly 18 to 43 kΩ. Raw traces before subtraction would help.
In Fig. S1, panels b to d are labelled VG = 0, 10 and 20 V, while the caption and text give "VG = −10, 0, and 20 V" (p. S3). Which gate voltages were measured, and how were they chosen?

For the diode effect, does η change sign as an abrupt jump at half-integer flux or as a smooth zero crossing, and how does η(Φ) in Fig. 1e, Fig. 3a and Fig. S2a compare with a trivial two-junction SQUID with a second harmonic, which also has zeros at integer and half-integer flux?

In Fig. 4l and Fig. S3l, how did you set the threshold on the third-derivative product that counts a gate voltage as a correlated peak, a correlated dip or no correlation, and how do the fractions change if you vary it?
